text: PTPTN education loans pay tuition fees and living costs for students at local higher education institutions only, meaning public institutions (IPTA) and private institutions (IPTS). Full-time diploma study is financed at IPTA, polytechnics and IPTS. Full-time first-degree (Ijazah Pertama) study is financed at IPTA and IPTS. Diploma Lanjutan is financed at IPTA and polytechnics. Part-time diploma and first-degree study at IPTS is financed only for students of five named private institutions: Universiti Terbuka Malaysia, Wawasan Open University, Asia e University, UNITAR and UNIRAZAK. Distance-learning (PJJ) diploma study is financed at IPTA only.
heading: Coverage by study level and institution

text: Foundation study at a private institution qualifies only at MMU, UNITEN, UTP, UNITAR and UNIRAZAK. A 2+1 twinning programme qualifies, but the loan covers only the years studied in Malaysia.
heading: Coverage by study level and institution

text: The applicant must be a Malaysian citizen aged 45 or below on the date of application, and must not have a PTPTN loan account that is being handled by a debt-collection agency (APH). The gross monthly income of the parents or guardian must not exceed RM50,000 after deducting RM250 for each dependant. The income limit has applied since 1 January 2024.
heading: Who can apply

text: The applicant must already hold an offer from an IPTA, IPTS or polytechnic, having met the entry requirements set by the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT) and MQA. The course must be approved by KPT and registered with PTPTN; only PTPTN-approved courses appear in the online application portal. At least one semester of study must remain at the time of application. The applicant must have opened a Simpan SSPN Prime or Simpan SSPN Plus account, and only a 15-digit SSPN Prime account can be used for the application.
heading: Admission offer and course conditions

text: Applications, results and offer letters are handled through myPTPTN. The loan starts from the semester in which the complete application is received, not from the first semester.
heading: Application channel

text: The maximum loan applies when the student or guardian is listed as a Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) recipient. Families not in the STR data with income up to RM8,000 receive 75% of the maximum, and those above RM8,000 receive 50% of the maximum.
heading: Loan tier by household income

text: An offer is valid for 14 days from approval. The signed, stamped agreement must be submitted within 14 days at the student's institution or the nearest PTPTN branch. The first payment is made after the complete agreement documents are received, and money is credited within 21 working days.
heading: After the offer
source_section: Pengeluaran Pinjaman Pendidikan; Penahanan Pengeluaran Pinjaman Pendidikan

text: Later payments require the student to remain active on the approved level, programme and institution and to have a GPA of at least 2.0 in the previous semester. Payment is withheld if the GPA is below 2.0, if study is deferred, or if the institution suspends the student. The loan is paid only into the student's own account, not to a parent.
heading: Continuing payments and withholding
source_section: Pengeluaran Pinjaman Pendidikan; Penahanan Pengeluaran Pinjaman Pendidikan

text: TESP is a MARA education loan for SPM, certificate (Sijil) and diploma leavers who continue to a diploma or a first degree in fields and local institutions approved by MARA.
heading: Purpose

text: The applicant and at least one parent must be Malaysian citizens with Bumiputera status. The student and parents or guardian must not be on MARA's blacklist. The applicant must not hold another sponsorship or financial aid for the same level of study. The course must be recognised by the Government and the relevant professional bodies. The applicant must not have had a previous sponsorship terminated for disciplinary reasons.
heading: Who can apply

text: The age limit is below 30 years for diploma study and below 40 years for bachelor's degree study. Priority is given to applicants from B40 and M40 households. The page gives no specific academic grade and no income figure; it says academic conditions follow the policy in force.
heading: Who can apply

text: This programme is only for outstanding graduates of MARA education institutions (IPMa) who continue to a diploma or first degree in Malaysia or overseas. Selection is based on academic excellence and active co-curricular involvement during certificate and diploma study at IPMa. The applicant and at least one parent must be Malaysian citizens with Bumiputera status, must not be on MARA's blacklist, and must not hold another sponsorship for the same level. The academic requirement is a CGPA of 3.90 or higher. Priority is given to the B40 group.
heading: Purpose and who can apply

text: The Kijang Pre-University Scholarship is for Malaysian citizens who have just completed SPM and are no older than 19 on 1 July 2026. The academic requirement is at least 8 As (A+ or A only) in the latest SPM, together with a CEFR result; the page does not define the CEFR level. Leadership, teamwork, co-curricular record and interpersonal skills are also assessed. The page does not state that an admission offer is needed before applying. Scholars study at pre-university colleges approved by BNM.
heading: Who can apply

text: The scholarship pays tuition fees, a subsistence allowance and related allowances. Moving on to undergraduate study depends on meeting the Kijang Undergraduate Programme requirements. After graduating, scholars serve BNM for two years for every year of study. Only shortlisted candidates are contacted.
heading: Benefits and obligations

text: The Kijang Undergraduate Scholarship is for Malaysian citizens no older than 22 on 1 July 2026 who have an offer to study at, or are already enrolled in, a university on BNM's approved list. For school leavers, one of these results is needed: STPM, diploma, matriculation or foundation CGPA of at least 3.50; A-Level with at least 3 As; or another listed international qualification. Applicants also need at least 5 credits in SPM or an equivalent, including Bahasa Melayu, English and Mathematics.
heading: Who can apply

text: Fields include economics, accounting, finance, actuarial science, mathematics, statistics, law, data science and computer science. Applications for the 2026 cycle were open from 17 to 26 April 2026; late applications are not accepted. The scholarship pays tuition fees, subsistence and related allowances, and scholars serve BNM for two years for every year of study.
heading: Fields, window and obligations

text: Dermasiswa B40 (DB40) 2026 is a JPA bursary for SPM 2025 candidates from low-income (B40) families who continue to diploma study in Malaysia. The applicant must be a Malaysian citizen who sat SPM 2025 for the first time, and must be under 19 (under 20 for students from the transition class) on 31 December of the exam year. Household per-capita income must be in the B40 category, which the statement gives as RM5,249 a month or less. The applicant must be free of chronic or infectious illness that could affect study, and neither the applicant nor the parents may be blacklisted by JPA or under JPA legal action.
heading: Who can apply
